x_1577958_dsb_pattern.name: Enterprise service management: workplace, facilities, legal, finance
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.overview: One front door, OOB department apps first, a template for the rest. (1) Employee Center with a single taxonomy covering IT, HR and the business departments. (2) Use the OOB department application where the client is licensed — Workplace Service Delivery (spaces, reservations, facilities cases), Legal Service Delivery (requests, matters, legal counsel centre), Finance/Accounts Payable operations. (3) For other departments, a standard onboarding template: department group(s), catalogue category, record producers onto an existing request/case table (or a single shared ESM scoped table approved once), SLAs, knowledge base, notifications and dashboard — no per-department custom tables. (4) Confidential departments (legal) get contextual security from the start. (5) Report per department and across the enterprise. Note custom-table licensing: each new table counts against App Engine entitlements.
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.pain: Each department runs its own inbox and spreadsheet Employees do not know where to go for non-IT help No workload, SLA or satisfaction data outside IT Departments buy point tools that duplicate the platform Facilities space and desk usage unknown after hybrid-work changes
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.summary: Business departments beyond IT — facilities, legal, finance, marketing — run their services from shared mailboxes and spreadsheets. Employees do not know where to ask, departments cannot show workload or SLA, and each team asks for its own tool. The pattern converges on one enterprise service model on the platform: OOB department applications where licensed (Workplace Service Delivery, Legal Service Delivery, Finance Operations), and a governed, templated case/request pattern for other departments, all behind Employee Center with a shared taxonomy.
